title: Destroy()
summary: Permanently removes an instance and disconnects its events. The instance becomes unusable: Parent is locked nil forever. For timed cleanup use Debris:AddItem instead of manual delays.

details.heading: Finality
details.body: A destroyed instance cannot be re-parented or revived. Its Parent property is sealed at nil, Changed fires one last time, and holding references just keeps a zombie object in memory.

details.heading: Destroy vs parent=nil
details.body: Setting Parent = nil merely detaches (the object remains usable and can return). Destroy is permanent and slightly cheaper for garbage collection.

explanation.whatItIs: The delete button — for instances that should never come back.
explanation.whyItExists: Games spawn endlessly; without destruction, memory and the hierarchy fill with garbage.
whenToUse: Finished effects, dead projectiles, consumed pickups
Replacing old objects with new ones
Timed removal via Debris:AddItem (preferred for simple cases)
whenNotToUse: Temporary hiding — parent to nil, or set Transparency/Enabled instead
Objects you might re-use — pool them
tips: Destroy connections too: disconnect stored RBXScriptConnections when their owner dies
Destroying a parent destroys the whole subtree
Never Destroy the Player or services' core objects
commonMistakes: Destroying but keeping variables pointing at the zombie — later ':IsA' etc. errors
Destroying on the client expecting server removal — destruction must happen where the instance is authoritative

examples.title: Clean projectile lifecycle
examples.code:
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")

local bullet = Instance.new("Part")
bullet.Parent = workspace
-- …fly…
Debris:AddItem(bullet, 5)      -- auto-Destroy after 5s

-- Manual equivalent:
-- task.delay(5, function() bullet:Destroy() end)
